detection.statement: A frozen board predicate identifies positions in which exactly one opponent non-pawn piece is legally capturable and has zero geometric defenders.
detection.evidence: 20.4% of 57,504 classifiable positions sampled from 60,000 unfiltered rated Lichess games (2013-01); 22.5% of 77,978 classifiable Lichess puzzle positions.
detection.robustness: 0.64% of T+ items flip to 'defended' under the Lichess ray-defence definition of is_defended.

recording.statement: Whether the player's move captured the designated target is recordable from the position and the move alone, with no engine, no result and no post-reveal information.
recording.evidence: research/measurement/predicates.py::observed_action; negative-controls.ts::outcomeLeakControl asserts an identical table after stripping every oracle field.

task_level_scoring.statement: Hit rate, false-alarm rate, sensitivity d' and response criterion c are computable for an item set under published formulae.
task_level_scoring.evidence: Stanislaw & Todorov (1999) with the Hautus (1995) loglinear correction; cross-language equivalence pinned by tests/research/measurement-sdt.test.ts.

scoring_inference.statement_refuted: B = capture(designated target) indicates use of the unprotected-piece discrimination.

generalisation_inference.statement_refuted: T+ and T- items are exchangeable on everything except the trigger.
